title: Resolver union still trails llms-aware on the frozen reviewed 20-site corpus after the OpenAPI search eligibility correction
claim: On the unchanged reviewed 20-site independent decision-quality corpus measured on 2026-08-28 after removing generic OpenAPI descriptions from search eligibility, llms-aware scored 89/100 and resolver-union scored 86/100. Resolver-union had 6 regret cases and 0 uniquely-correct union cases.
scope: The frozen ARWP 20-site independent decision-quality corpus and the committed 2026-08-28 OpenAPI-search-eligibility measurement only. This is an engineering benchmark of reviewed intent selection, not a representative survey of the web or a claim about answer quality, search ranking, latency or token cost.
doesNotProve: that llms.txt is universally the best web discovery mechanism
that the 20-site corpus represents the web or market adoption
that resolver-union has the same score against later human-reviewed ground-truth revisions
that benchmark accuracy predicts LLM answer quality, SEO ranking, latency or token savings

evidence.description: Committed dated benchmark result records 89/100 llms-aware, 86/100 resolver-union, 6 regret cases, 0 uniquely-correct union cases and unchanged reviewed ground truth.
Decision-quality policy explains resolver regret, the unchanged-ground-truth rule and why resolver-union remains experimental after the correction.
R4 dominance epic tracks the same current frozen-corpus gate and broader external trust criteria.

notes: The older 81/100 resolver-union value is preserved as historical evidence from before the general OpenAPI search eligibility correction; it is not the current post-correction baseline for this claim.
Potential live publisher capability drift is queued for human review separately and must not silently mutate this frozen measurement.
